verdict.rationale: Metorial documents OAuth user authorization and describes Portals as 'branded places' where users connect integrations, which glancingly touches the branding half of the story. Per-environment 'authentication configs' are mentioned, but nothing shows customers can supply their own OAuth client ID/secret or fully white-label the consent flow. Missing for 10: explicit bring-your-own OAuth app credentials, documented custom branding controls for the authorization screens (logo, domain, removal of Metorial branding), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can white-label the authorization flow with my own branding and my own OAuth app credentials

citations.quote: Portals are branded places where users discover and connect approved integrations, skills, and MCP access.
OAuth lets your users authorize access to their accounts on services like Slack, GitHub, Google Calendar, and more.
Each environment has its own provider deployments, API keys, authentication configs, and logs
